name: Design task workflow & status visualization
description:
## Conversation Summary

The user identified that as codx-junior agents generate and update large numbers of tasks simultaneously, it becomes increasingly difficult for users to track work status and know when their input is needed. The existing UI primitives (Kanban boards, Desktop tabs, Wall, EventBar) were analyzed as a foundation. Three design proposals were defined: **Mission Control** (live three-lane swimlane board with a slide-in detail panel), **Command Center** (inbox + chronological timeline model inspired by GitHub/Slack), and **Focus Mode HUD** (an ambient overlay bar that sits on top of the existing Kanban without replacing it). Each proposal was then implemented as a **fully interactive HTML + Tailwind CSS mockup** with realistic simulated data, live agent animations, reply flows, and working UI state transitions.

messages.content:
@biblio 
As agents imporve the workin with codx-junior chats/tasks it becomes more difficult for the user to follow with the work done/status.

We already have  some components to visualize tasks and organize them but is not possible for a human to manage the amount of tasks generated.

We need to find a way where codx-junior project manager agent keeps tasks organized and communicvates with the users; and a way where users can interact with the agents while having a clear view of current status and follow up with tasks that require their attention. 

The Desktop component allow users to have multiple tabs open but that's really bad way of following with work flow and usually user focus on one or two tasks at a time.

Having a summary and kind of "wall" of work done/progress and a side detail view where open an event/chat is an option.

Current task organization is based on Kanban boards, investigate and come out with 3 design proposals on how to allow users to follow with workflow/events/tasks going on and allow user to jump in the loop to interact with it.

There'll be a background agent llistenning to tasks events and taking actions to ensure iasks are always updated and organized, but that's out of the scope right now.

Now I have a thorough understanding of the existing system. Let me compose the design proposals document.

---

# codx-junior — Workflow Visibility & User Interaction: 3 Design Proposals

## Context & Current State

### What exists today

The current UI is built around these key primitives:

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| **KanbanContainer / Kanban.vue** | Primary task organization via boards, columns, and `TaskCard` items |
| **Desktop / DesktopView** | Dockview-based multi-tab panel layout — flexible but cognitively noisy |
| **Wall.vue** | Grid of `ChatPreview` cards sorted by `last_update` — recent activity surface |
| **EventBar.vue** | Status-bar widget showing `lastEvent` text from `session.events` |
| **NotificationControl.vue** | Grouped info/warning/error notification badges in the top bar |
| **StatuBar / TopBar** | Shell chrome hosting EventBar and user info |
| **session.js events** | Socket-driven event stream: task updates, AI messages, file writes |
| **chats.js** | All tasks/chats as flat objects with `column`, `board`, `updated_at`, `updating` flags |

### The core problem

Agents can generate and update dozens of tasks simultaneously. The user:
- **cannot see** what agents are doing without opening individual chat tabs
- **cannot triage** which tasks need human input without scanning every board
- **gets overwhelmed** by the Desktop tab model when work fans out across many tasks
- has **no clear signal** for "this task needs me now" vs "agent is handling it"

---

## Proposal 1 — Mission Control (Live Activity Wall + Slide-in Detail)

> *"A NASA-style operations view where all active work is visible at a glance, and the user drills in only when needed."*

### Layout

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TOP BAR  [Project ▼]          [🔴 2 🟡 5 🟢 12]  [User]   │
├──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│          │  MISSION CONTROL — Live Feed                     │
│  LEFT    │ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌────────────┐  │
│  RAIL    │ │ 🔴 NEEDS YOU │ │ 🟡 IN PROG │ │ 🟢 DONE   │  │
│          │ │  TaskCard    │ │  TaskCard   │ │ TaskCard  │  │
│  Board   │ │  TaskCard    │ │  TaskCard   │ │ TaskCard  │  │
│  Filter  │ │  [+ new]     │ │  ...        │ │ ...       │  │
│          │ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └───────────┘   │
│  Agents  │                                                   │
│  Status  │  ── Recent Events ─────────────────────────────  │
│          │  [14:02] agent:backend  saved routes.py          │
│  Pinned  │  [14:01] agent:frontend generated ChatView       │
│  Boards  │  [14:00] user:@you     ← waiting for review      │
│          │                                                   │
└──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          ← slides in from right →
                          ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                          │  DETAIL PANEL  [×]               │
                          │  📋 TaskCard title               │
                          │  Status: 🟡 In Progress          │
                          │  Agent: backend-dev              │
                          │  ─────────────────────           │
                          │  Chat / message thread           │
                          │  [Type a message…]  [Send]       │
                          └──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Design Decisions

**Left Rail — Contextual Navigation**
- Collapsible list of boards with task count badges
- Active agent indicators per board (pulsing dot when agent is writing)
- Pinned boards float to the top

**Center — Three-lane Live Board**
- Tasks auto-sorted into three swim lanes driven by a computed `attention` flag:
  - 🔴 **Needs Your Input** — agent paused, question posed, or `stuck` flag set
  - 🟡 **In Progress** — `updating: true` in `chats.js`, agent actively working
  - 🟢 **Done / Idle** — `updating: false`, column is "done" / "review"
- Cards live-animate between lanes as agent state changes (Vue transition groups)
- Cards show: task name, board, last agent message snippet, time elapsed, profile avatar

**Bottom — Live Event Ticker**
- Scrolling log fed directly from `session.events`
- Each event is clickable → opens the detail panel for that task
- Color-coded by type: agent action (blue), user mention (yellow), error (red)

**Right — Slide-in Detail Panel**
- Opens on card click, overlays ~40% width without leaving the view
- Full `ChatView` embedded — user can reply directly
- Close returns focus to the live board
- Keyboard shortcut: `Esc` to close, `J/K` to navigate between tasks needing attention

### What gets reused

- `TaskCard.vue` / `TaskCardLite.vue` — the card rendering
- `Wall.vue` — the ChatPreview pattern for the event log
- `EventBar.vue` — feeds the ticker
- `ChatView.vue` — embedded in the detail panel
- `session.events` + `chats.updating` — drive the live lane sorting

### Strengths
- Zero learning curve — familiar Kanban visual language
- User is never more than one click from interacting
- Agents working silently stay out of the way (green lane)

### Weaknesses
- Three-lane model may not map cleanly to complex multi-board setups
- Detail panel needs careful width management on smaller screens

---

## Proposal 2 — Command Center (Timeline + Inbox Model)

> *"Inspired by GitHub notifications + Slack channels — a persistent inbox of events that need attention, with a timeline of everything happening."*

### Layout

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TOP BAR   [Project ▼]   📥 Inbox (3)   📜 Timeline   [User]    │
├────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    │                                              │
│   📥 INBOX         │   📜 ACTIVITY TIMELINE                      │
│   ─────────────    │   ──────────────────────────────────────    │
│                    │                                              │
│  🔴 Review PR      │  14:05 ●────── agent:backend               │
│     board: api     │         └ wrote 3 files in task "Auth fix" │
│     2 min ago      │                                              │
│                    │  14:03 ●────── agent:frontend               │
│  🔴 Ambiguous req  │         └ asked: "Which API endpoint?"      │
│     board: ui      │         └ [→ task paused — needs input]    │
│     5 min ago      │                                              │
│                    │  14:01 ●────── user:you                     │
│  🟡 Running: Auth  │         └ created task "Add OAuth"          │
│     board: backend │                                              │
│     8 min ago      │  14:00 ●────── agent:planner                │
│                    │         └ created 5 sub-tasks               │
│  [+ New Task]      │         └ assigned to: frontend, backend   │
│                    │                                              │
│                    │  [Load more…]                               │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    On inbox item click:
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  MODAL / SIDE PANEL — "Review PR"       │
        │  Board: api  |  Column: Review          │
        │  Agent: backend-dev  |  Status: Waiting │
        │  ─────────────────────────────────────  │
        │  [Last message from agent…]             │
        │  ─────────────────────────────────────  │
        │  [Reply…]              [Mark resolved]  │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Design Decisions

**Inbox (Left panel)**
- Aggregates only tasks that require human attention: agent paused, error state, PR ready for review, or explicitly `@mentioned`
- Sorted by urgency then recency
- Badge count in the top bar acts as a persistent attention signal (like email unread count)
- "Mark resolved" removes from inbox, moves task to next column automatically
- User can reply directly from the inbox item — no navigation required

**Timeline (Right panel)**
- Chronological log of all agent + user actions across all projects/boards
- Groups related events under a collapsible agent "session" (e.g., all actions in one task run)
- Each event has a direct link icon to open the relevant task
- Filterable by: project, agent profile, event type (created / modified / asked / completed)
- Auto-scrolls to live events; user can pause auto-scroll to review history

**Task interaction modal**
- Opens as a focused overlay (not a full tab replacement)
- Shows the chat thread, current status, assigned agent, files modified
- Action buttons: Reply, Reassign Agent, Mark Done, Move Column
- Keyboard: `Enter` to reply, `R` to mark resolved, `N` for next inbox item

### Interaction Flow Example

```
1. Agent pauses, adds "@user: should this use REST or GraphQL?"
2. Inbox badge increments: 📥 Inbox (3) → (4)
3. User clicks inbox item
4. Modal opens with conversation thread visible
5. User types reply, hits Enter
6. Agent resumes, inbox item moves to "In Progress" indicator
7. When done, task auto-archives from inbox
```

### What gets reused

- `NotificationControl.vue` — extended to become the Inbox badge
- `session.events` — feeds the Timeline
- `ChatView.vue` — embedded in the modal
- `TaskCard.vue` — summary view inside inbox items
- `chats.js` — `updating` flag drives In Progress indicators

### Strengths
- Maps to a familiar mental model (email inbox / GitHub notifications)
- Inbox gives a clear, bounded list of "things I must do"
- Timeline gives full historical audit trail of all agent work
- Works well for users managing multiple projects simultaneously

### Weaknesses
- Two-panel layout requires more horizontal space
- Users need to understand the inbox/timeline separation initially
- Timeline can get very noisy on busy projects without good filtering

---

## Proposal 3 — Focus Mode (Agent Dashboard + Contextual HUD)

> *"An always-on heads-up display that lives alongside any view — no mode switching required. Inspired by IDE status bars and VS Code's problem panel."*

### Layout — Normal view (Kanban stays primary)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TOP BAR  [Project ▼]    [⚡ 3 agents active]     [User]        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│        EXISTING KANBAN BOARD (unchanged)                         │
│                                                                  │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐        │
│  │ Backlog  │  │ In Prog  │  │ Review   │  │  Done    │        │
│  │          │  │ ⚡TaskA  │  │ 👁 TaskB │  │ ✓ TaskC  │        │
│  │          │  │ ⚡TaskD  │  │          │  │ ✓ TaskE  │        │
│  └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘        │
│                                                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  HUD BAR  ▼ (collapsible)                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ 🤖 agent:backend   TaskA  "Writing auth middleware…"    │    │
│  │ 🤖 agent:frontend  TaskD  "Generating component…"  ●●● │    │
│  │ 👁 NEEDS YOU       TaskB  "Which design pattern?"  [→] │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STATUS BAR  [14:05 agent:backend saved routes.py]  [🔴1 🟡2]  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Layout — HUD expanded (split view)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TOP BAR                                                         │
├────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┤
│                            │  AGENT DASHBOARD                   │
│   KANBAN BOARD             │  ─────────────────────────────     │
│   (shrinks but stays       │  Active Agents (3)                 │
│    visible)                │  ┌──────────────────────────────┐  │
│                            │  │ 🤖 backend-dev               │  │
│                            │  │   TaskA: Auth middleware      │  │
│                            │  │   ████████░░░░  Writing...   │  │
│                            │  │   [View Chat]  [Pause]       │  │
│                            │  ├──────────────────────────────┤  │
│                            │  │ 🤖 frontend-dev              │  │
│                            │  │   TaskD: Modal component      │  │
│                            │  │   ██████████░░  Almost done  │  │
│                            │  │   [View Chat]  [Pause]       │  │
│                            │  ├──────────────────────────────┤  │
│                            │  │ 🔴 WAITING — needs input     │  │
│                            │  │   TaskB: API design decision  │  │
│                            │  │   Agent asked 3 min ago       │  │
│                            │  │   [Open & Reply]             │  │
│                            │  └──────────────────────────────┘  │
│                            │                                     │
│                            │  Summary Today                      │
│                            │  ✓ 12 tasks completed              │
│                            │  📝 34 files modified              │
│                            │  💬 7 conversations                │
└────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Design Decisions

**HUD Bar — always visible, collapsible**
- Docked to the bottom of any view — Kanban, Desktop, Wall, anywhere
- Shows only **actively running** tasks and **tasks needing input** (max ~5 rows)
- Each row: agent avatar + name, task name, live streaming message snippet, action button
- Expand button opens the Agent Dashboard as a right panel (uses the existing `Splitter.vue`)
- Collapse returns to current view without losing context

**Agent Dashboard — right panel, on demand**
- Per-agent "cards" with:
  - Current task name and board
  - Live progress indicator (streaming dots or progress bar)
  - Last AI message snippet
  - `[View Chat]` — opens chat inline at the bottom of the card (mini thread)
  - `[Pause]` / `[Resume]` — agent control
- "Needs Your Input" section floats to the top, visually separated in red/warning
- Daily summary metrics (tasks done, files touched, conversations) at the bottom

**TaskCard enhancement — inline agent badges**
- Existing Kanban cards get a small ⚡ indicator when an agent is actively working on them (using the existing `updating` flag from `TaskCard.vue`)
- No full layout change — the Kanban remains the user's primary mental model

**Status Bar enhancement**
- Existing `StatuBar.vue` / `EventBar.vue` extended with a mini agent count badge `[⚡ 3 active]`
- Clicking it toggles the HUD bar open/closed
- Notification badges (existing `NotificationControl.vue`) stay as-is

### Interaction Flow Example

```
1. User is viewing Kanban board normally
2. HUD bar at bottom shows: "🤖 backend  TaskA  Writing routes..."
3. A second row appears: "🔴 NEEDS YOU  TaskB  [Open & Reply]"
4. User clicks [Open & Reply] in the HUD
5. A mini chat panel expands in-place within the HUD
6. User replies, HUD row changes to "🟡 agent resumed"
7. User never left the Kanban view
```

### What gets reused

- `StatuBar.vue` / `EventBar.vue` — extended, not replaced
- `TaskCard.vue` — `updating` computed property already exists
- `Splitter.vue` — provides the resizable panel split
- `ChatView.vue` — embedded in the agent card "mini thread"
- `session.lastEvent` / `session.events` — feeds HUD live text

### Strengths
- **Least disruptive** — Kanban stays the primary view, no learning curve
- HUD is unobtrusive but always present — no "where is my task" problem
- Scales well: collapsed HUD = zero overhead; expanded dashboard = full visibility
- Reuses the most existing components

### Weaknesses
- HUD can feel cramped if many agents run simultaneously
- Progress bar metaphor may be misleading for open-ended AI tasks
- Requires agents to expose a structured "current action" signal to the frontend

---

## Comparison Summary

| Feature | Proposal 1 — Mission Control | Proposal 2 — Command Center | Proposal 3 — Focus Mode HUD |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Primary metaphor** | Live Kanban swimlanes | Inbox + Timeline | Ambient HUD overlay |
| **Disruption to current UX** | Medium (new view) | Medium (new view) | Low (addon to existing) |
| **Best for** | Ops-focused power users | Multi-project managers | Developers staying in flow |
| **Needs-input signal** | 🔴 lane, always visible | Inbox badge + count | HUD row + status bar badge |
| **History / audit** | Event ticker | Full timeline | Status bar events only |
| **User interaction** | Slide-in detail panel | Modal overlay | Inline mini-chat in HUD |
| **Mobile friendly** | Yes (swimlane stacks) | Partially (inbox only) | Yes (HUD collapses to bar) |
| **Agent status** | Lane position + card pulse | Timeline grouped by agent | Per-agent card with live text |
| **Reuse of existing code** | High | Medium | Very High |
| **Implementation effort** | Medium | High | Low–Medium |

---

## Recommended Starting Point

**Start with Proposal 3 (Focus Mode HUD)** as the foundation — it requires the least structural change, builds directly on `StatuBar`, `EventBar`, `Splitter`, and `TaskCard`, and delivers immediate value (users can see what agents are doing without changing their workflow).

**Layer in Proposal 1's swimlane view** as an alternative "Mission Control" tab/view accessible from the main menu — giving power users a dedicated ops screen when they want full visibility.

**Proposal 2's Inbox concept** can be implemented as an extension to `NotificationControl.vue` — promoting task-linked notifications (not just text strings) into actionable inbox items with reply capability.

This phased approach ships value incrementally without requiring a full UX overhaul.

history.summary:
# Conversation Summary

1. **Problem Context**: As codx-junior agents improve, the volume of chats/tasks grows exponentially, making it difficult for users to track work status and progress.

2. **Current Limitations**: Existing task visualization components and Kanban boards are insufficient; multi-tab navigation doesn't support effective workflow management as users typically focus on only 1-2 tasks simultaneously.

3. **Proposed Solution Architecture**: Implement a project manager agent that organizes tasks and communicates with users, paired with an improved UI showing task summaries and a "wall of work" displaying progress and completed items.

4. **Design Request**: Develop 3 design proposals for a workflow/task tracking interface that provides a clear summary view with side-detail panels, allowing users to jump into agent interactions while maintaining visibility of ongoing events.

5. **Scope Clarification**: A background agent will handle task event listening and updates to keep tasks organized, but this functionality is out of scope for the current design phase.

> **Workflow Visibility & Human-Agent Interaction Design Proposals**
>
> As codx-junior agents handle increasing numbers of tasks, users struggle to track progress and know when their input is needed. The current UI — built on Kanban boards, a multi-tab Desktop, and a basic event bar — lacks a clear signal for "agent working" vs "needs me now". Three design proposals were explored: **Mission Control** (a live three-lane swimlane wall with a slide-in detail panel), **Command Center** (an inbox + chronological activity timeline model), and **Focus Mode HUD** (a non-intrusive always-on bar docked to any existing view). The recommendation is to ship the HUD first as it reuses the most existing components with minimal disruption, then layer in the Mission Control view and an actionable Inbox on top. Together these give users ambient awareness of all agent activity while keeping human interaction to a focused, low-friction "jump in when needed" model.

## Conversation Summary

The user identified that as codx-junior agents generate and update large numbers of tasks simultaneously, it becomes increasingly difficult for users to track work status and know when their input is needed. The existing UI primitives (Kanban boards, Desktop tabs, Wall, EventBar) were analyzed as a foundation. Three design proposals were defined: **Mission Control** (live three-lane swimlane board with a slide-in detail panel), **Command Center** (inbox + chronological timeline model inspired by GitHub/Slack), and **Focus Mode HUD** (an ambient overlay bar that sits on top of the existing Kanban without replacing it). Each proposal was then implemented as a **fully interactive HTML + Tailwind CSS mockup** with realistic simulated data, live agent animations, reply flows, and working UI state transitions.
